methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two information sources.
mindtraced_atomic_units: FSM to receive and validate data bytes from a serial communication stream
Serial protocol uses one start bit (0), 8 data bits (LSB first), and one stop bit (1)
Assert a 'done' signal when a valid stop bit is detected
'out_byte' is only valid when 'done' is asserted
If the stop bit is missing, enter an error recovery state
Continuously monitor the input for a valid stop bit in error recovery
Incorporate a timeout mechanism to prevent indefinite waiting in error recovery
module top_module ( input clk, input in, input reset, output [7:0] out_byte, output done )
spec_atomic_units: top_module has inputs: clk, in, reset
top_module has outputs: out_byte[7:0], done
out_byte is only valid when done is asserted
combinational logic generates out_byte based on serial data (in) and FSM state
done signal is generated based on the FSM's state
combinational logic acts as a decoder for the current state to determine the output values
When FSM is in the valid stop bit state, out_byte is assigned the value of the received data byte
When FSM is not in the valid stop bit state, the value of out_byte is a don't-care
done signal is asserted when the FSM is in the state where a valid stop bit has been received
done signal is de-asserted when the FSM is in any other state
State Decoding Logic decodes the current state of the FSM to determine whether a valid stop bit has been received
out_byte Assignment Logic assigns the received data byte to the out_byte output when the state decoding logic indicates a valid stop bit
done Signal Assignment Logic assigns the done signal to 1 when the state decoding logic indicates a valid stop bit, and to 0 otherwise
Minimize the delay from the FSM's state to the out_byte and done outputs
valid_byte_received signal from the FSM indicates whether a complete and valid byte has been received
data_bits[7:0] are the source for the out_byte value
If valid_byte_received is asserted, then out_byte[7:0] = data_bits[7:0]
If valid_byte_received is de-asserted, then out_byte[7:0] is a don't-care
If valid_byte_received is asserted, then done = 1
If valid_byte_received is de-asserted, then done = 0
Minimize the delay from the valid_byte_received signal to the out_byte and done outputs
Care should be taken to prevent glitches on the done signal
The FSM will likely have several states: Idle, Start Bit Detected, Receiving Data (8 states), Stop Bit Verification, and potentially an Error state
The state transitions occur on the rising edge of the clock (clk)
The reset signal, when asserted high, synchronously resets the FSM to the Idle state
